name: Cinema Museum
hero_subtitle: An indoor pause on Ouarzazate’s film identity — quieter than the outdoor studios.

overview.title: Props, Posters and the Local Film Story
overview.p1: The Cinema Museum gathers costumes, posters, models and the story of how this desert town became a base for international shoots. It is compact, shaded and useful if you want context without committing to a full Atlas Studios tour.
overview.p2: Families and film fans get the most from it. If your trip is only about ksars and palms, you can skip it without regret.
overview.p3: Check opening hours — they are not the same as a kasbah you can walk into at dawn.

q1.question: Is there a ticket?
q1.answer: Yes — modest; pay at the entrance.

q3.question: Same as Atlas Studios?
q3.answer: No — this is a museum, not a walk through outdoor sets.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Cinema Museum?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for history and safe paths on fragile mud brick.

q5.question: Is Cinema Museum suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes with supervision on steps, rooftops and uneven ground.

food.title: Café after the museum
food.p1: No full restaurant inside. Step out for tea or lunch in the centre afterward.
food.p2: Keep the museum for the exhibits; eat in town.
food.li3: Hotel café if you want quiet
food.li5: Combine with Taourirt the same morning

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Cinema Museum

1.title: Hours first
1.desc: Confirm opening times before you walk across town — museums here do not run on kasbah logic.

2.title: Combine
2.desc: Excellent with Kasbah Taourirt in one morning: outdoor walls then indoor film story.

3.title: Kids
3.desc: Props and posters hold attention better than a long studio tour for some children.
